nodes.name: Co0.9Fe0.1-Se/NF electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: CoCl₂ (1.62 mmol), SeO₂ (1.80 mmol) and KCl (9 mmol) were dissolved into 60 mL DI water and stirred vigorously to form a homogeneous solution. Then, FeSO₄ (0.18 mmol) was added into it to form a precursor solution for the electrodeposition. The electrodeposition process was conducted in a three-electrode system, in which the nickel foam served as the working electrode and a graphite rod as well as a saturated calomel electrode (SCE) served as a counter electrode and a reference electrode, respectively. The Co₀.₉Fe₀.₁–Se were deposited onto the nickel foam via a constant potential -0.7 V versus the SCE for 30 min.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP shows actual Co:Fe ratio consistent with precursor solution and M/Se ratio ~1:1.25.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ICP technique was used to analyze the actual compositions of as-synthesized materials and the results were presented in Table S1. The ratio of M/Se (M represents the content of Fe and Co) is ~ 1:1.25 in all materials containing Co...

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows diffraction peaks at 33.7°, 44.9°, 59.7°, 62.7° assigned to (101), (102), (103), (201) planes of CoSe phase (PDF# 89–2004).
nodes.evidence_snippet: For Co0.9Fe0.1-Se/NF and Co-Se/NF, the diffraction peaks at 33.7°, 44.9°, 59.7°, 62.7° could be assigned to the (101), (102), (103) and (201) planes of CoSe, according with the PDF# 89–2004.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows porous and shaggy structure with plenty of channels and interspaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Co0.9Fe0.1-Se/NF exhibits a porous and shaggy structure with plenty of channels and interspaces.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows nanoparticles with diameters of ~5-10 nm dispersed onto nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM and high-resolution TEM images were used to further scrutinize the fine structures... the nanoparticles with diameters of ∼5−10 nm are dispersed onto the nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringes with interplanar spacing of 2.65 Å attributed to (101) plane of CoSe, with co-existence of crystalline and amorphous regions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the lattice fringes with interplanar spacing of 2.65 Å can be observed (Fig. 1f), which can be attributed to the (101) plane of CoSe. Notably, there are also some amorphous areas around the crystal.

properties.description: High-resolution TEM image showing amorphous and crystalline regions

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED shows diffraction spots for (101), (102), (110), (103) planes of CoSe and halo indicating amorphous structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the diffraction spots in the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern (the inset of Fig. 1f) could be assigned to the typical crystal planes of (101), (102), (110) and (103) for CoSe. The halo in SAED pattern also indicates a part of amorphous structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS confirms presence of Co, Fe, Se, O elements with homogeneous distribution shown by elemental mappings.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDS spectrum suggests the existence of the elements Co, Fe, Se and O in the nanostructure (Fig. S3). By EDS elemental mappings analysis, it further reveals the homogeneous distribution of the elements Co, Fe, Se and O.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Co 2p peaks at 778.9 eV (CoSe), 780.9 eV (Co-O), 784.1 eV satellite (Co(II)); O 1s at 531.2 eV (surface oxide), 533.6 eV (adsorbed water); Se 3d at 55.4 eV (CoSe), 59.7 eV (Se oxidation); Fe 2p at 714.2 eV (Fe3+).
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS is performed to further identify the chemical states... Co 2p high-resolution XPS spectrum displays three different Co species. The peak at 778.9 eV could be assigned to the Co in CoSe... Fe 2p peak region at 714.2 eV could be assigned to Fe3+.
